chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Bayhaqi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Suli informed us. He said: Harun ibn Abdullah al-Muhallibi narrated to me. He said: Di`bil ibn Ali al-Khuza`i narrated to us. He said:
The news of the death of Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) came to me while I was staying in Qum. So I composed this ra-rhymed ode of mine:

I see that [Bani] Umayya are excused if they kill, But I see no excuse for Bani al-Abbas. Sons of Harb, Marwan, and their kin, Bani Mu`ayt — masters of hatred and grudges. You are a people who killed their first for [protecting] Islam, Until when they came to power, they went all the way to disbelief.

Head to Tus, to the grave of the pure one there, If you are one who seeks fulfillment through religion. There are two graves in Tus — the best of all people, And the grave of the worst of them — this is a lesson.

The impure cannot benefit from nearness to the pure, Nor is the pure harmed by the nearness of the impure. Far be it! Every soul is pledged for what its own hands have earned — So take what you wish, or leave it.

key_terms.الرائية: A qasida whose rhyme ends in the letter ra' (ر)
key_terms.الرجس: The impure/filthy one — here referring to Harun al-Rashid, who is buried near Imam al-Rida in Tus
key_terms.الزكي: The pure/righteous one — here referring to Imam al-Rida (AS)
key_terms.رهن: Pledged/mortgaged — each soul is held accountable (pledged) for its own deeds

ai.seo_question: What poem did Di`bil al-Khuza`i compose upon the death of Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This hadith records the elegy composed by the poet Di`bil al-Khuza`i upon hearing of the death of Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) while he was in Qum. The poem contrasts the buried Imam — the best of people — with the grave of the Caliph Harun al-Rashid also interred at Tus, drawing a profound lesson about the spiritual irrelevance of physical proximity between the pure and the impure. It concludes with a Quranic echo that every soul is answerable for its own deeds, not for who lies nearby.

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Husayn b. Ahmad al-Bayhaqi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-Suli informed us. He said: Harun b. `Abdullah al-Mahlabi narrated to me. He said: De`bal b. `Ali al-Khuza`i narrated to us. He said:
When I was staying in Qum, the news of the death of `Ali b. Musa al-Rida (as) came to me. So, I said this visionary poem:

I see that [Bani] Umayya are excused if they kill, But I see no excuse for Bani al-`Abbas. Sons of Harb, Marwan, and their kin, Bani Mu`it are the masters of hatred and grudges, The firsts of them were killed upon Islam, Once they came to power, they were able to disbelieve [again].
Head to Tus, to the grave of the pure, If you were there, you would find two graves in Tus, The best of all the people, and the grave of the worst of them. This is a lesson
that impurity cannot benefit from nearness to purity, Nor can the pure be harmed by nearness to impurity. No way! Every soul will reap what its hands sow, So, harvest what you wish, or sow a seed.
